note:
The size of the widget set, as a number somebody has to sign for. Admission has always been per-widget -- D1 and D2 are asked of one candidate at a time -- and nothing owned the total, so the set grew from 39 to 51 in three days while a refactor to shrink it sat unexecuted. Every one of those twelve passed its own review honestly. That is the failure this file exists to stop: not a bad widget, but a total nobody was accountable for. It is a ratchet in the pattern ontology/coupling-debt.json and widgets/check-coverage.json already use: the count may fall freely and may not rise unless this file is updated in the same commit, with the admission review that justifies the addition named. Raising it is allowed. Raising it silently is not. Split into two numbers on 2026-10-12: a widget costs code, a release, a lab check and an audit sweep against twelve criteria, while a retired widget costs none of that and a bundled composition costs a JSON file whose members already carry all of it. 'widgets' is the maintenance number -- live and unretired -- and 'addable' is the attention number a practitioner experiences. Reduction must move the first without growing the second, which is the difference between reduction and relabelling.

PENDING WIDGETS ARE EXEMPT, 2026-10-12, on the practitioner's rule. A widget that is pending because of merge activity -- not developed, not used -- does not count, precisely because it is emergent: we do not yet know whether it deserves to be a tree in that forest (above and below), nor whether it fills a value gap in the inventory (sideways). Counting a candidate against a target for the committed set makes the number mean two things at once.

The state already existed and was inert. implementationStatus 'proposed' has been a permitted value since the release format was written and exactly one line read it -- the line checking that the value is permitted. This is the same pattern 'retired' was in until it was made to take effect earlier today.

What stops this being a parking lot: a pending widget must name what it REPLACES, so it cannot be a way to add capability for free; the exemption ends when the widget is developed and an example uses it, which is the practitioner's own two-part condition; and it carries a clock, because 'in flight' is a transient state and nine of the twelve widgets added between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 went from added to independently checked within three days. A merge in flight for a fortnight is not in flight.

Three populations were measured before choosing this one, and the two obvious readings were both wrong. Exempting widgets with no lab check would have exempted isochrone, nearest, access and facilities -- the untested set is the OLDEST widgets, five first released 2026-10-06, and isochrone is the centre of the John Snow example. It is untested because an independent check is hard, not because its value is in doubt. Exempting widgets no example exercises would have exempted measure_area and reproject. Neither predicate picks out what 'emergent' means.

target.basis: docs/experiments/64-widget-streamlining.md, whose phases retire nine example-bound widgets, one duplicate display and collapse three nearest-neighbour implementations into one.
target.note: A target, not a ceiling. D1 says primitives are exposed when a workflow needs them and not in advance, so a needed primitive is not refused by arithmetic -- it is recorded.

output, places and centers retired -- the first three this project has retired. All three were already superseded with working adapters; what was missing is that implementationStatus 'retired' had no effect anywhere.

pendingRule.criterion: Pending because of merge activity, not developed, and not used.
pendingRule.declaredBy: implementationStatus 'proposed' in the widget's current release, plus an entry below.
exemptFrom: widgets/check-coverage.json -- an undeveloped widget owes no lab check
the add palette and node search -- there is nothing to add
mustDeclare: what it replaces, so a pending widget cannot add capability for free
pendingRule.endsWhen: The widget is developed AND a worked example uses it. At that point it counts, and what it replaces must be retired in the same commit.
pendingRule.clockBasis: Nine of the twelve widgets added between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 were independently checked within three days. A merge in flight for a fortnight is not in flight; it is a widget nobody is building.

ladder.statedBy: The practitioner, 2026-10-12: "Used in a worked example is one form of testing. Comparing it with notebook is another. More worked examples for widget means more use. Field testing even better."
rungs: declared only -- it exists and nothing else
example use -- n worked examples, and n times the evidence
notebook parity -- an independent recomputation agrees, or a declared reason none applies
field use -- a practitioner used it on real work
ladder.measuredBy: scripts/widget-evidence.mjs, derived into widgets/evidence.json and checked for drift by validate:evidence.
ladder.whyThisMatters: "Tested" was the wrong shape, and both readings of it were wrong. Exempting widgets with no notebook check would have exempted isochrone, nearest, access and facilities -- the unchecked set is the OLDEST widgets, and isochrone is the centre of a worked example, unchecked because an independent check is hard rather than because its value is in doubt. Exempting widgets no example uses would have exempted reproject and measure_area. They are different axes and a widget can be strong on one and weak on the other.
ladder.fieldUse: Zero widgets, of 48. Declared and empty on purpose: an empty top rung is a measurement, a missing one is a flattering omission.
ladder.bottomRungNote: Used by no worked example and still owing a notebook check. This is the population the pending exemption is about, and it is four widgets rather than the thirteen or twelve the two single-axis readings would have exempted.
ladder.alsoFound: No worked example carries a composition node at all. compute_walking_catchment is the one bundled composition and nothing exercises it, and its four members have zero example uses because the isochrone example still uses the isochrone composite rather than its decomposition. A decomposition was built, a composition shipped from it, and no example uses either.
